checked_sources: Independent exact MIS dynamic program and pairwise ball check, /mnt/data/scope09_science_checks.py
correctness.rationale: Each length-five word has a deletion ball of distinct length-four traces. The condition that no pair of different words shares two traces is exactly an independent-set condition in the 32-vertex conflict graph. Exhaustively reconstructing all 496 pairs yields 305 shared-trace intersections of size 0, 142 of size 1 and 49 of size 2. A fresh independent memoized include/exclude exact MIS recurrence explored all branches and obtained maximum 20 and one maximizer; the repo provides an independently structured Bron–Kerbosch maximal-clique search as a second bound method. The unique 20-word witness meets the original deletion-ball predicate, reversal/complement invariance and weight profile (1,3,6,6,3,1). Finite exhaustion is a complete proof for the fixed 32-word universe, not extrapolated asymptotics.
residual_risks: The uniqueness is for labeled codes, not just modulo coordinate symmetries; only binary length five and distinct reads.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Different asymptotic quantifiers and constructive families leave this finite exact labeled optimality undetermined. Asymptotic bounds and Levenshtein-type reconstruction theorems do not imply exact 20/unique at n=5.

value.rationale: Fixed two-read reconstruction is a foundational channel-design setting; the exact first small nontrivial labeled optimum and uniqueness supply a natural short-block benchmark and test instance, beyond a mere list of known codewords.
residual_risks: Finite n=5 theorem does not generalize automatically; value is a complete natural parameter case, not an asymptotic improvement.

final_claim: For binary length-five words under two distinct single-deletion reads, the optimal reconstruction code has exactly 20 words, and the maximizing labeled code is unique; its 49-edge conflict graph has a unique independent set of size 20, stable under complement and reversal.
limitations: Not deletion-error-correcting one-read codes or other reading channels; no extension to n>5.
